content.title: Celebrity Deaths 2026: In Memoriam Gallery
content.text: Throughout 2026 we will continue to update this IN MEMORIAM photo gallery with notable celebrity deaths from film, television, theater and music. The year started in the first two months with the sad news of the deaths of Oscar winner Robert Duvall, Emmy winner Catherine O'Hara, Rock and Roll Hall of Fame member Bob Weir (of The Grateful Dead), actor Eric Dane, and former teen superstar James Van Der Beek. Major entertainment figures honored in the 2025 gallery were double Oscar winner Gene Hackman, Oscar champ Diane Keaton, legendary director and actor Robert Redford, Emmy winner Loretta Swit, music legends Roberta Flack, Sam Moore, Ozzy Osbourne, Sly Stone, Brian Wilson, and Peter Yarrow, sports announcer and actor Bob Uecker, and Oscar nominated actor Terence Stamp, actresses Diane Ladd and Joan Plowright, and directors David Lynch and Rob Reiner. Photo : Michael Buckner/Getty ImagesValerie PerrineActress Valerie Perrine died on March 23 at age 82. She was an Oscar and Golden Globe nominee for Lenny and also starred in Superman, Superman II, The Slaughterhouse Five, and The Electric Horseman.Photo : Jason Merritt/Getty ImagesChuck NorrisActor and martial arts champion Chuck Norris died on March 19 at age 86. He starred in action films Breaker! Breaker!, Lone Wolf McQuade, Missing in Action, Delta Force, and Code of Silence. He was also known for his long-running TV series Walker: Texas Ranger.Neil SedakaLegendary singer and songwriter Neil Sedaka died on Feb. 27 at age 87. He had three #1 hits on the Billboard charts: “Breaking Up Is Hard to Do,” “Laughter in the Rain,” and “Bad Blood.” Other hits included “Calendar Girl,” “Lonely Night,” and “Love Will Keep Us Together.” He was inducted into the Songwriters Hall of Fame in 1983 and was a five-time Grammy nominee.Photo : Michael Buckner/PMCEric DaneActor Eric Dane died at age 53 on Feb. 19. He starred for several seasons on Grey’s Anatomy and more recently on Euphoria. In the early part of his career, he appeared on Saved By the Bell, The Wonder Years, Married.. with Children, Roseanne, and Charmed.Photo : WWDRobert DuvallActor Robert Duvall died on Feb. 15 at age 95. He was an Oscar winner for Tender Mercies and received six other nominations for The Godfather, The Great Santini, The Apostle, Apocalypse Now, A Civil Action, and The Judge. He also won two Emmys for Broken Trail and received nominations for Lonesome Dove, The Man Who Captured Eichmann, and Stalin.Photo : Kevin Winter/Getty ImagesJames Van Der BeekActor James Van Der Beek died at age 48 on Feb. 11. He became a young superstar on the teen dramedy Dawson’s Creek and followed that success with CSI: Cyber and Pose. Films included Varsity Blues, Texas Rangers, The Rules of Attraction, and Labor Day.Photo : David Livingston/Getty ImagesBud CortActor Bud Cort died on Feb. 11 at age 77. His best known film role was in Harold and Maude opposite Ruth Gordon. Other top movies included M*A*S*H, Brewster McCloud, Heat, Dogma, Coyote Ugly, and Pollock.Photo : Ethan Miller/Getty ImagesCatherine O’HaraActress Catherine O’Hara died on Jan. 30 at age 71. She was an Emmy winner for writing on SCTV and acting for comedy series Schitt’s Creek. She also received nominations for Temple Grandin, The Last of Us, and The Studio. Her best known films included Beetlejuice, Home Alone, Waiting for Guffman, Best in Show, and For Your Consideration,Photo : NBC Television/Courtesy of Getty ImagesDemond WilsonActor Demond Wilson died on Jan. 30 at age 79. He was best known for his long-running role opposite Redd Foxx on Sanford and Son. He also starred on The New Odd Couple and had many guest roles on TV shows.Photo : Neilson Barnard/Getty ImagesBob WeirBob Weir, founding member of The Grateful Dead, died on Jan. 10 at age 78. The band was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 1994 and was selected for the Kennedy Center Honors in 2024.
